text:
olivia: kicking off canary rollout for release v2.14.3 -> prod, starting at 10% traffic. observability gate enabled. rolling over 12:05 UTC :rocket:
deploy-bot: started rollout v2.14.3 (canary=10%) target: embed-service, route: prod-us-west, preflight checks passed
monitoring-bot: SLO check OK for last 30m (error_rate < 0.5%, p95 latency < 200ms) — baseline stable
mike: noted. i'll watch p95 and 5xx dashboards, will ping on spikes
sanjay: quick FYI — release notes link: https://internal/redwood/releases/v2.14.3
elaine: small change: added kv-cache tweak and updated batching config. should reduce token cost but watch latency variance.
jamal: can we keep canary at 10% for at least 15m before shifting? last time we saw a delayed latency bump at ~12m
olivia: yes planning 15m stable window then 50% followed by 100% if green
monitoring-bot: alert rule deployed: canary-slo-watch-us-west: triggers if p95 > 250ms for 3/5m OR 5xx rate > 0.8% over 5m
mike: 4m in — p95 steady ~185ms, 5xx 0.12%
sanjay: seeing a small error cluster from embed-service at 12:18:29, spike to 0.9% (1 minute). looks like an outlier request pattern. logs:
```
embed-service | 2026-03-20T12:18:29Z | ERROR | downstream timeout cid=abc123 path=/v1/encode
```
monitoring-bot: alert fired: canary-slo-watch-us-west at 12:18:30 — 5xx rate 0.9%
olivia: saw the alert. holding traffic shift. setting canary traffic to 0%? or keep at 10% and analyze?
jamal: i'd keep 10% for now, root-cause might be transient. let's throttle new connections to affected hosts and watch for recurrence.
elaine: agree with jamal — keep 10%. also pin canary to v2.14.3 (no automatic further shifts) until we triage.
mike: digging into traces — most errors are timeouts to S3-ish blob store used by embed pipeline in us-west-2a. latency to blobstore spiked ~45s around the error window.
olivia: ok that's infra vs code. set a postmortem ticket and notify infra. if we see repeat spike (>2 alerts in 10m) we rollback.
sanjay: created ticket INFRA-4821 and added traces + sample request ids. tagging infra-team.
monitoring-bot: escalation sent to #eng-infra and #oncall at 12:24:05
deploy-bot: paused scheduled traffic shift to 50% (manual hold by olivia) — canary remains at 10%
mike: for visibility, adding a temporary dashboard panel for per-host SLOs and KV cache hit ratio — will post link shortly
elaine: also rolling back the batch-size tweak in a hotfix branch so we can test if that was compounding timeouts. not deploying without infra green.
jamal: thumbs up. if infra confirms external blobstore instability, we can proceed with traffic shift after they stabilize and we see 30m of green.
olivia: agreed. final call: hold canary at 10%, pin version, infra to investigate, rollback if >2 alerts in 10m. i'll update release notes and ops channel. :white_check_mark:
monitoring-bot: summary: canary paused at 10% due to transient 5xx spike; alerts sent; ticket INFRA-4821; next check scheduled 12:45 UTC
deploy-bot: rollback ready if requested — use `/deploy rollback prod embed-service v2.14.2 --reason "canary 5xx spike"`
mike: will monitor and report back. tagging @sre on the traces.
olivia: thanks team — keeping thread here. will unpause when infra confirms stable or if no further alerts by 12:45. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
